title: NBER-Based U.S. Recession Indicator
revision_note: NBER's Business Cycle Dating Committee dates recession peaks and troughs 4 to 21 months after the fact; a month recorded as expansion can later be reclassified as recession once NBER announces a new dating.
methodology: Contiguous runs of USREC = 1 are collapsed into {start, end} recession intervals, both the first and last recession month. An ongoing recession has end = null.
This is a standalone, chart-agnostic dataset reused for recession shading across multiple charts (spreads today; Fed Funds, real rate, ERP and credit spreads planned).
notes: Reflects only officially NBER-dated recessions, which are announced with a lag (see revision_note); a current downturn may not yet appear here even if it is later dated as a recession.
Months are assigned to the 1st of the month.
